newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prosecutors say ready to quit Daimler probe.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors say ready to quit Daimler probe.

text.p: Stuttgart prosecutors said on Friday they would quit their investigation into alleged insider trading by Daimler-Benz AG management board chairman Eckhard Cordes on condition he paid a fine.

The investigation centred around comments Cordes made to a small group journalists in early March at the Geneva car show where he provided details of Daimler's financial results before they were officially made public.
"The prosecutors office believes there is only a negligible amount of guilt and ultimately, no damage was done," a spokesman for the prosecutors' office said.
According to the spokesman, Cordes had signalled his willingness to pay a fine of over 10,000 marks to charity.
The Daimler management board member had told journalists the company would report net profit of more than two billion marks and sales would total around 107 billion marks in 1996.
The profit figure he cited was well above analysts' expectations and Daimler's share price rose by more than 3.5 percent the next day.
Daimler went on to report group net income of 2.8 billion marks for 1996.

The Federal Securities Supervision Authority, or BAWe, originally filed a complaint against Cordes and questioned whether the profit disclosure should have come via a so-called "ad-hoc" electronic transmission, which German law requires for potentially market-moving information.
Failure to report via the "ad-hoc" route has sometimes constituted a violation of Germany's insider trading rules. --Scott Miller, Bonn Newsroom + 49 228 260 97150
